hypothesis: A shared neural scorer over supplied sparse associative memories can use demonstrations of rule families absent from optimization. Test its added value against written and ordinary neural controls.
architecture: Enumerate subsets of <=3 of n binary coordinates. Supplied counts, label means and consistency statistics form external memory. The network learns a scalar trust score per subset from query-answer BCE only. No hidden rule labels are input.
pooled_baseline: A separate end-to-end DeepSets support encoder plus query decoder, fixed 8-bit width; same episodes and query supervision.

development.allowed_selection: train and validation only, both from known families

selection: maximize validation query accuracy, then minimize validation BCE; freeze final budget/code/run list before opening final predictions
baselines: minimum-error then minimum-arity symbolic subset selector
stress: one and eight corrupted support labels
limits: A 256-neuron source subgraph plus artificial adapters, not a whole fly brain.
Sparse feature enumeration and associative retrieval are supplied algorithms, not learned.
Unseen functions are restricted to <=3 relevant Boolean inputs; parity4 is explicitly outside that class.
No natural language understanding, arbitrary Python generation, biological intelligence claim, or hidden oracle fallback.
